seg_confusion_table — SEGMENTATION score op

• Data kinds: labels2d × labels2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.seg_confusion_table(labels_pred, labels_true, *, background: 'int' = 0) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import segeval; segeval.seg_confusion_table(labels_pred, labels_true, *, background: 'int' = 0) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("seg_confusion_table"))

Usage

Label-correspondence contingency table (rows = truth, columns = prediction) with max-overlap matching and a uniqueness flag (seg_confusion_table).

table[i, j] = number of pixels that carry both the true label labels_true[i] and the predicted label labels_pred[j]. Correspondence is by maximum overlap: the partner of true i = among the non-background columns, the one where table[i, :] is largest (pred_of_true, a label value, −1 if none); the partner of prediction j = the largest non-background row (true_of_pred). mutual_true[i] = the partner of true i picks true i back, mutual_pred[j] likewise. claims[j] = number of true objects that chose prediction j as partner. unique_matching = all non-background rows and columns choose each other mutually (= a 1-to-1 bijection). Background rows and columns stay in the table but are excluded from the correspondence. It is argmax, not Hungarian (assignment maximising the sum), so several true objects may pick 1 large prediction — that is what claims ≥ 2 signals.

Returns: table, labels_true / labels_pred (label values of rows and columns), row_sums / col_sums, pred_of_true / true_of_pred, mutual_true / mutual_pred, claims, unique_matching, n_true / n_pred (counts excluding background), n.
